answer: Every ballot enters the orchard on probation. Each seals its claim in a vault with a $25 bond, then waits 28 tides — seven days, the window optimistic rollups give watchers — while any single peer may post a fraud proof against it. The dispute narrows by bisection, halving it until one bad step stands exposed. A farm cloning one forged root into 10,000 ballots dies by the fraud-proof check: one proof against the shared root slashes all 10,000 bonds at once, $250,000 lost, and the challenger keeps half. One honest echo fells the whole orchard of fakes for one proof.
